sections.title: The Inner Petals

sections.fact: Rose petals overlap in layers, helping protect the flower's inner parts while the bud is still closed.

sections.title: The Outer Bloom

sections.fact: Different rose varieties can have very different numbers of petals, from simple flowers with five petals to very full blooms with many layers.

sections.title: The Stem

sections.fact: The sharp points on rose stems are technically called prickles rather than thorns because they grow from the stem's outer layer.

sections.title: The Leaves
sections.learn: Finish with dots 54 through 66 to shape the leaves and complete the rose. Check that every number is connected before adding colour.
sections.fact: Rose leaves often have toothed edges, which means their margins look like a row of tiny teeth.
